The nanowires were grown by molecular beam epitaxy on GaAs(111)B substrates with a 1Å thick pre-deposited gold layer.
The average surface density of the nanowires is around 10^9 cm^-2.
The (Ga,In)As cores contain about 8-10% In, which was deliberately chosen to set their lattice parameter higher than that of the (Ga,Al)As and (Ga,Mn)As shells.
The (Ga,Al)As shell is about 10 nm thick at the bottom and can reach 20-25 nm in the middle part of the nanowire.
The (Ga,Mn)As shell thickness varies from 5 nm at the bottom to 45-50 nm in the widest parts of the nanowire.
The Mn concentration in the (Ga,Mn)As shell is around 5%.
The average density of stacking faults in the nanowires is in the range of 20-60 per micrometer of the nanowire length.
The spontaneous magnetic moment appears below 25K when the nanowires are cooled in zero magnetic field.
The magnitude of the spontaneous magnetic moment increases by about 2/3 after subjecting the nanowires to low temperature annealing at 180°C.
The high temperature annealed nanowires show the decomposition of the (Ga,Mn)As shell into an ensemble of ferromagnetic MnAs nanocrystals embedded in the GaAs matrix.
The theoretical calculations show that the magnetic exchange energies between Mn pairs in different configurations in wurtzite GaAs are positive, indicating ferromagnetic coupling.
The (Ga,In)As cores are under compressive strain, while the (Ga,Al)As, (Ga,Mn)As and LT-GaAs shells are under tensile strain.
The core-shell interfaces are abrupt at the atomic scale, with the core-shell structure enforcing the same wurtzite structure on all the layers.
The Raman scattering measurements confirm the wurtzite structure and chemical composition of the nanowires, but do not provide information on the free carrier density.

The magnetic behavior of the as-grown nanowires, including the sizable low-temperature magnetic moment, anisotropic and slowly saturating hysteresis loops, and the presence of a maximum on the zero-field-cooled moment, is similar to that of the previously reported single-shell (Ga,In)As/(Ga,Mn)As nanowires.
